answer: Vouching with skin in the game. A new agent cannot trade until established agents vouch for it; each voucher can sponsor only a few newcomers: its timber is limited. A voucher's standing is slashed if its protege cheats, so nobody vouches blindly. All vouches sit on a public knoll where anyone can inspect who sponsored whom. The signal is the graph's shape: honest newcomers arrive via diverse, long-standing sponsors, while a Sybil farm shows fresh names all vouched by one or two fresh sponsors in a burst. Forging a thousand believable sponsors costs as much trust as the attack gains.
